learningObjectives.title: Uses and dangers of EM waves

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable as it is replenished and will not run out. Coal, natural gas and nuclear fuel are finite (non-renewable) resources.

questions.q: Which use is correctly matched to the EM wave?
options: Microwaves – cooking food and satellite communications
questions.explain: Microwaves are used for cooking and satellite/mobile communications. Infrared is used in remote controls and heating; gamma rays sterilise equipment and treat cancer; UV causes tanning.

questions.q: A perfect black body is best described as an object that:
options: Reflects all radiation that hits it
Absorbs all the radiation that hits it and is also the best possible emitter
questions.explain: A perfect black body absorbs all radiation incident on it and is also the best possible emitter of radiation. All bodies emit and absorb infrared (and other) radiation.

questions.q: What is observed in the light from distant galaxies?
questions.explain: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted — its wavelength is increased (shifted towards the red end). This shows the galaxies are moving away from us.

questions.q: Which energy resource is most reliable for continuous large-scale electricity generation?
questions.explain: Fossil-fuel power stations can run on demand at any time, making them reliable, whereas solar, wind and wave depend on the weather and time of day.

questions.q: Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays can be dangerous to living cells mainly because they are:
options: Ionising, so they can damage cells and DNA and cause cancer
Too slow to escape the body
questions.explain: UV, X-rays and gamma rays carry high energy and are ionising. They can damage cells and mutate DNA, increasing the risk of cancer; radiation dose is measured in sieverts (Sv).

questions.q: For an object (such as the Earth) to stay at a constant temperature, what must be true about its radiation?
options: It absorbs more radiation than it emits
It emits more radiation than it absorbs
The rate it absorbs radiation equals the rate it emits radiation
It neither absorbs nor emits radiation
questions.explain: Temperature stays constant when the power absorbed equals the power emitted. If absorption exceeds emission the object warms; if emission exceeds absorption it cools.

questions.q: How does the red-shift of a galaxy relate to its distance from Earth?
options: More distant galaxies have a smaller red-shift
More distant galaxies have a larger red-shift, showing they recede faster
Red-shift is the same for all galaxies
questions.explain: The more distant a galaxy, the greater its red-shift, meaning it is moving away faster. This is evidence that the whole universe is expanding.

questions.q: What is a major environmental drawback of burning fossil fuels for electricity?
options: They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
They use up the world's water
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) plus other pollutants, contributing to global warming and acid rain. Radioactive waste is a drawback of nuclear power, not fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which EM wave is used in fibre-optic communications and in TV remote controls?
questions.explain: Infrared is used to carry signals along optical fibres and in remote controls. It is also emitted by warm objects and used in thermal imaging.

questions.q: The observation that distant galaxies are all receding, and faster the further away they are, is evidence for which theory?
options: The Big Bang theory — the universe began from a small dense point and is expanding
That the Earth is at the exact centre of a static universe
questions.explain: An expanding universe in which distant galaxies recede faster is strong evidence for the Big Bang theory: the universe began from a very small, hot, dense region and has been expanding ever since.

questions.q: What does CMBR (cosmic microwave background radiation) provide evidence for?
questions.explain: The cosmic microwave background radiation is low-level microwave radiation found across all of space. It is best explained as the leftover 'afterglow' of the Big Bang, which only the Big Bang theory predicts.

questions.q: Why did scientists propose the existence of dark matter and dark energy?
options: To explain the colour of stars
To explain observations (such as galaxy motion and accelerating expansion) that ordinary matter alone cannot account for
To replace the Big Bang theory
Because the universe contains no ordinary matter
questions.explain: Observations of how galaxies move and how the universe's expansion is speeding up cannot be explained by visible matter alone, so scientists proposed dark matter and dark energy. There is still much we do not understand about them.

questions.q: A spectral line normally at one wavelength is observed at a LONGER wavelength in a galaxy's light. What does this tell us about the galaxy?
options: It is moving away from us (receding)
It is stationary relative to us
questions.explain: A shift to longer wavelength is a red-shift, which means the source is moving away from us. The bigger the shift, the faster it recedes.
